lean.name: OAI.SKValueG.hamCoeff_distance
lean.note: Scalar proof tree: squared distance of H_n coefficients is n(1-R₁₂²), the convention in increment form. No ξ and no extra Gaussian appear.

statements.markdown:
For overlap $R_{12}=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_i^1\sigma_i^2$, the covariance is
$nR_{12}^2/2-1/2$. Thus the convention is $\xi(t)=t^2/2$, with
$\xi''=1$. A centered Gaussian of variance $1/2$, common to all
configurations, removes the final constant and leaves the expected maximum
unchanged.

statements.markdown:
At a minimizer, the separate contact and diffusion arguments establish
the fixed-strip inputs and eventual positivity. First take the mesh
limit to obtain $I(T)\le P_*$, then let $T\uparrow1$. The scalar
terminal assembly identifies that last limit with $\mathcal P(\gamma)$.
Together with $P_*\le\mathcal P(\gamma)$ this proves equality.
The third scalar endpoint constructs its own diffusion before making
this application. These sources therefore supply an independent route
to the equality, alongside the imported Parisi formula in §6.

lean.note: Scalar model. The energy increment variance n−nR², which is the stated covariance in distance form.

statements.markdown:
We use the covariance convention $\xi(t)=t^2/2$, so $\xi''=1$.
Adding one independent centred Gaussian of variance $1/2$ to every
configuration's energy gives covariance $n\xi(R)$ and leaves the
expected maximum unchanged, which is the normalisation of the
ground-state Parisi formula of [Auffinger and Chen (2017), Theorem 1][AC].

lean.note: Scalar model. Spins are Bool read through spin. Couplings are indexed by all ordered pairs; only i<j enter.

lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinHamiltonian
lean.note: The same Hamiltonian, as written in the support model.

statements.markdown:
For independent standard Gaussian couplings $J_{ij}$, the pure,
zero-field [Sherrington–Kirkpatrick (SK) Hamiltonian][SK] is
$$
H_n(\sigma)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j,
\qquad \sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n.
$$

statements.markdown:
With the maximisation convention, its limiting ground-state energy per
spin is
$$
P_*:=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\mathbb E\max_\sigma H_n(\sigma).
$$
